newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel trades steady, Russian scarce.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel trades steady, Russian scarce.

text.p: European straight-run fuel changed hands at steady prices on Tuesday while good quality Russian material continued scarce, traders said.
A cargo of good quality low sulphur straight-run from Britain was bought by a French major for a little over $105 a tonne fob, in line with yesterday's deal out of Scandinavia.
Some traders said they expected low sulphur prices to soften slightly into next week even if crude holds at current levels, with adequate supply seen up to mid-June.
Others felt poor margins for refinery distillation units would keep straight-run attractive.
"In the slightly longer term it depends on run cuts. Initial distillation margins are negative but upgrading units are still positive so we may see straight-run a bit stronger," said one dealer.

Good quality Russian was scarce and well bid. An M-40 was heard traded to a British major on Tuesday for around three means flat while a straight-run M100 was being offered for around two means plus $7 today and was sold.
